# Mortar Smash (mortarsmash.com)

> Mortar Smash (formerly titled Brickworks) is a free, plain-English guide for people interested in bricks: brick history, standard brick sizes (UK, US, German, Australian), bond patterns, how clay bricks are made, famous brick buildings, and how to care for and repoint brickwork. It also offers a free brick and mortar calculator and an original brick-smashing browser game of the same name. All text and graphics are original.

## Guide
- [Brick guide (home)](https://mortarsmash.com/): Overview of everything on the site, with an answer-first summary and FAQ.
- [A short history of bricks](https://mortarsmash.com/#history): From sun-dried mud bricks through fired brick, the Romans and the Industrial Revolution.
- [Brick types and sizes](https://mortarsmash.com/#types): Common, facing, engineering, fire, handmade and perforated bricks, plus a table of national standard sizes.
- [Brick bonds and patterns](https://mortarsmash.com/#bonds): Stretcher, English, Flemish and stack bond, with diagrams.
- [How bricks are made](https://mortarsmash.com/#making): The six steps from digging clay to kiln firing and sorting.
- [Famous brick buildings](https://mortarsmash.com/#famous): Malbork Castle, Hampton Court, the Great Mosque of Djenné, Chilehaus, St Pancras and the Ctesiphon arch.
- [Brick care and repointing tips](https://mortarsmash.com/#care): Mortar choice, raking out, curing, gentle cleaning and fixing damp at the source.
- [Brick FAQ](https://mortarsmash.com/#faq): Short answers on brick sizes, English versus Flemish bond, brickmaking and repointing mortar.

## Tools
- [Brick calculator](https://mortarsmash.com/brick-calculator.html): Estimates bricks, wet mortar, cement and sand for a wall in UK, US modular, German NF, Australian or custom sizes, and shows the working. Includes one-click common-project presets, a "bricks for common jobs" table, and a US answer block on how many bricks per square foot (modular ~6.9/sq ft single leaf; 20 ft × 3 ft two-wythe seat wall worked example), and a brick pier and pillar calculator (UK 1½-brick pier ~4½ bricks per course, ~60 per metre; US modular 12 and 16 in piers), and a brick-on-edge coping section (~13⅓ UK bricks per metre on a 215 mm wall; US rowlock cap ~4.6 per ft), and a garden wall footing concrete section (~0.1 m³ per metre for a 215 mm wall on a 450 × 225 mm strip; US 16 × 8 in footing ~0.9 cu ft per ft), and a concrete block section (~10 UK 440 × 215 mm blocks per m²; US 8 × 8 × 16 in CMU 1.125 per sq ft).
- [Mortar calculator](https://mortarsmash.com/mortar-calculator.html): Wet mortar, cement and sand from a brick count or wall area (UK, US modular, German NF, Australian). About 0.3 m³ wet mortar, five 25 kg cement bags and ~0.5 t sand per 1,000 UK bricks in a half-brick wall at 1:4 with 10% waste; per-1,000 and per-m² table; mix ratio guide (1:3 to 1:6, US Types N/S/M).

## Game
- [Mortar Smash](https://mortarsmash.com/game.html): A free, original brick-smashing arcade game with 9 levels and keyboard, mouse and touch controls.
